t: Declared illegitimate at two when her mother, Anne Boleyn, was executed, and imprisoned under her Catholic half-sister Mary, Elizabeth came to the throne in 1558 at the age of 25.

She established an English church with the monarch as supreme governor, never married or named an heir, kept Mary, Queen of Scots, captive for nineteen years before sanctioning her execution, and fought a long war with Spain.

Her 44 years on the throne gave England stability and a sense of national identity, though recent historians point to military failures, the tactics of her forces in Ireland and the economic troubles of her last years.
dyk: Elizabeth translated Latin and Greek authors throughout her life. A translation of the Annals of Tacitus in Lambeth Palace Library was confirmed as her own in 2019, after a detailed analysis of the handwriting and paper.
ev: Elizabeth is born at Greenwich Palace, the daughter of Henry VIII and his second wife, Anne Boleyn
After Wyatt's rebellion against her half-sister Mary she is imprisoned in the Tower of London and then held under house arrest at Woodstock
Mary dies on 17 November and Elizabeth becomes queen at the age of 25
A new Act of Supremacy makes her Supreme Governor of the Church of England, and an Act of Uniformity makes church attendance compulsory
Pope Pius V issues the bull Regnans in Excelsis, declaring her excommunicated and releasing her subjects from allegiance
Mary, Queen of Scots, held in England for nineteen years, is beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle
The Spanish Armada is dispersed by English fire ships off Gravelines, and Elizabeth addresses her troops at Tilbury
Elizabeth dies at Richmond Palace aged 69, and James VI of Scotland is proclaimed king of England

f.born: 7 September 1533 at Greenwich Palace; daughter of Henry VIII of the House of Tudor and his second wife, Anne Boleyn
f.died: 24 March 1603 at Richmond Palace, aged 69, between two and three in the morning, after an illness and a severe depression; interred in Westminster Abbey
f.role: Queen of England and Ireland from 17 November 1558 until her death in 1603; Supreme Governor of the Church of England from 1559
f.known: the Elizabethan Religious Settlement; never marrying, as the "Virgin Queen"; the imprisonment and execution of Mary, Queen of Scots; the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588; the speech to the troops at Tilbury; the Elizabethan era of Shakespeare and Marlowe; the charter of the East India Company; 44 years on the throne
